result.reason: Clarity: A is sectioned under plain headings (Performance / What changed / fee change) with a proper date and addressee block, so the fee change is findable at a glance; it defines the comparison index (40/30/20/10), states that the 5% commodity weight remains inside the 4%-12% policy range, and limits the fee change explicitly to the Real Assets sleeve with core equity and bond fees unchanged. B presents the same content as four dense unheaded paragraphs, buries the fee change mid-letter, leaves the index undefined, does not say whether the commodity weight is within range, and never bounds the increase to one sleeve - the obvious client question. Tone: the clients are a pipeline engineer and a reservoir engineer who want technical, brief statements and no generalities. A is declarative and unpadded ('We raised listed infrastructure to 44% of the sleeve from 38%') and names the fee increase directly. B adds softening filler ('Our portfolio construction evolved during this quarter to capture specific market opportunities,' 'Looking at the broader picture,' 'For context') and hedges the increase as 'an adjustment,' which reads as marketing rather than reporting to this audience. A also closes with an offer to walk through the positioning or the fee; B has no such invitation despite serving as contractual notice. A wins on both dimensions; its extra length is structure and scope-limiting detail rather than padding.
